category_title: Child with profound multiple learning difficulties and visual impairment
minimal_context: The tutor is reading a storybook with sound buttons to Leah while she sits in her wheelchair at 5pm.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is 5pm. Let's sit here in your wheelchair and read the Gruffalo book.

STUDENT: (Frowns) Ah.

TUTOR: I will press the buttons to make the noises of the animals.

STUDENT: (Says the word repetitively while continuing to frown) Ah. Ah.

TUTOR: Let's keep going with the story. Listen to this part.

STUDENT: (Vocalisations gradually become louder and more persistent, demonstrating she is unhappy and uncomfortable in her wheelchair) Ah! Ah!

options.A: Sit next to the student on the floor, use the sound-button book, and use the puppet to engage in physical play by jiggling her arms, stroking her back, and holding her hand.
options.B: Make expectations clear while also making it known that the tutor wants to hear what the student has to say, ensuring this is done respectfully rather than as a 'gotcha' moment.
options.C: Articulate the alternatives the student confronts and the actions taken, using comments such as, 'I see you made the decision to focus here,' or 'How can you change this to a better decision?'
options.D: Use a digital reading app on a tablet where every single word of the story flashes up on the screen for the student to follow during the session.
